outcome: I can choose indicative or subjunctive and distinguish present from prior action.
explanation: Indicative forms generally present information as asserted; subjunctive forms occur in constructions expressing desire, evaluation, doubt or necessity. Je doute qu'il vienne means I doubt he will come, while je sais qu'il vient asserts that he is coming. Present subjunctive can refer to now or later. Past subjunctive combines subjunctive avoir/être with a past participle to mark prior completion: je suis content qu'elle soit venue means I am glad she came. Certain constructions, such as bien que (although), require subjunctive even for a factual event, so meaning alone is not a complete rule.

For a real future possibility, si takes present rather than future. Peut-être (perhaps), il est probable que (it is likely that) and il est possible que (it is possible that) express different certainty; the last normally introduces subjunctive, while probable affirmative normally takes indicative.
